openings.claim: Couple the known insertion stop A to clamp B through contact-gated tightening: restraint begins only after the rod reaches its stop. This might prevent the tighter-fit return error without altering either rod.
openings.delta: Change the assembly dependency from independent tightening to seat-then-tighten. Propose two adjustable plywood rod saddles with fixed end stops, hand-tightened M5 restraint, and cord/elastic retention of every loosened component. Geometry within 90 mm and retention remain fabrication questions.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: ordinary additive benefit from a stop plus tighter restraint. Coupling predicts lower pointer displacement for intact A×B than for identical parents with tightening performed before stop contact. For lateral displacement d, test whether 7−dAB exceeds (7−dA)+(7−dB), and whether breaking the sequence removes that excess. These are proposed comparisons, not measured synergy; exchange repeatability could disagree.
openings.probe: Use supplied 7 mm loose-joint displacement as baseline. In the intact configuration, compare A alone with restraint released, B alone with stop contact bypassed, and intact A×B, allocating four load trials across these modes. In the second configuration retain every parent component but break only the seating-to-tightening interface; allocate four load trials. Run twelve exchanges per configuration: five of each original rod, then two replacing the 19 mm rod with 18 mm. Log return error, ten-second 10 N displacement, exchange time, initial setup and readjustment burden. Parent-only modes provide load screening, not full exchange validation. If release modes count as extra configurations, this comparison exceeds the cap and cannot proceed as specified.
assumptions: Six plywood pieces and supplied hardware can form two retained saddles within the envelope; unverified.
Square end contacts remain reproducible across supplied size variation; unverified.
Defeat: no interaction beyond additive benefit, broken interface performs equally, any return exceeds 2 mm, load escape, exchange reaches forty seconds, or fabrication/testing exceeds 100/20 minutes.
Capacity to complete screening plus exchanges within twenty minutes is unknown; the stop cap alone establishes no informative feasible test.

assessment: A bounded coupling hypothesis merits fabrication review. No deployment or target performance is established; resource geometry, retention, mode counting and test capacity remain unresolved.
